learningObjectives.title: Internal energy, specific heat capacity and latent heat
Particle motion in gases and pressure

questions.q: Which equation is used to calculate the density of a material?
questions.explain: Density is defined as the mass of a substance divided by the volume it occupies.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of density?
questions.explain: Density is mass (kg) divided by volume (m³), giving kilograms per cubic metre.

questions.q: Solids are usually much denser than gases. This is mainly because in a solid the particles are:
questions.explain: Particles in a solid are packed closely, so more mass is contained in the same volume than in a gas.

questions.q: A block has a mass of 600 kg and a volume of 0.2 m³. What is its density?
questions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume = 600 ÷ 0.2 = 3000 kg/m³.

questions.q: In a solid, the particles are best described as:
options: arranged in a regular fixed pattern, vibrating about fixed positions
arranged randomly and moving quickly in all directions
far apart with no forces between them
questions.explain: Solid particles are held in a regular arrangement by strong forces and only vibrate in place.

questions.q: When ice melts to form water, the mass of the substance:
questions.explain: A change of state is a physical change in which mass is conserved.

questions.q: A liquid has a density of 1000 kg/m³. What is the mass of 0.5 m³ of this liquid?
questions.explain: Mass = density × volume = 1000 × 0.5 = 500 kg.

questions.q: The internal energy of a system is:
options: the total kinetic and potential energy of all its particles
the energy needed to raise its temperature by 1°C
only the kinetic energy of its particles
the heat it gives off to the surroundings
questions.explain: Internal energy is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies stored by the particles in a system.

questions.q: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the energy needed to:
options: raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1°C
change the state of 1 kg without changing its temperature
raise the temperature of any mass by 1°C
questions.explain: Specific heat capacity is the energy required per kilogram to raise the temperature by one degree Celsius.

questions.q: Which equation gives the energy needed to change the temperature of a substance?
questions.explain: Energy transferred equals mass × specific heat capacity × change in temperature.

questions.q: How much energy is needed to heat 2 kg of water (specific heat capacity 4200 J/kg°C) by 10°C?
While a pure substance is boiling, its temperature:
questions.explain: During a change of state the energy supplied changes the state rather than raising the temperature.

questions.q: Which equation gives the energy needed to change the state of a substance?
questions.explain: Energy for a change of state equals mass × specific latent heat.

questions.q: The specific latent heat of fusion is the energy needed to change 1 kg of a substance from:
options: solid to liquid with no change in temperature
liquid to gas with no change in temperature
solid to liquid while raising its temperature by 1°C
gas to liquid while cooling it
questions.explain: Latent heat of fusion is the energy per kilogram to melt a substance at constant temperature.

questions.q: During melting, the energy supplied to a substance is used mainly to:
options: break the forces between particles, increasing their potential energy
increase the kinetic energy and temperature of the particles
increase the mass of the substance
questions.explain: Latent heat raises the particles' potential energy by overcoming the forces between them, so the temperature stays constant.

questions.q: How much energy is needed to melt 0.5 kg of a substance with a specific latent heat of fusion of 340 000 J/kg?
The pressure a gas exerts on the walls of its container is caused by:
options: the weight of the gas pressing down
questions.explain: Gas pressure results from the force exerted as randomly moving particles collide with the container walls.

questions.q: When a gas is heated so that it becomes hotter, its particles:
options: move faster, with greater average kinetic energy
questions.explain: Raising the temperature increases the average kinetic energy, so the particles move faster.

questions.q: For a fixed mass of gas held at constant volume, increasing the temperature will:
options: have no effect on the pressure
turn the gas into a liquid
questions.explain: Faster particles collide with the walls more often and harder, so the pressure rises.

questions.q: When a gas is compressed quickly, work is done on the gas. This causes its:
options: internal energy and temperature to increase
questions.explain: Doing work on a gas transfers energy to its particles, raising the internal energy and temperature.
